title: The Lamb that was slain (Apocalypse 5)
hookLine: the Mass joins this heavenly liturgy (CCC 1090)

cards: In Handel's Messiah, audiences stand for the Hallelujah chorus, but it isn't the ending. The Hallelujah closes the second part.
The whole work ends later, with a slower, larger chorus and then an Amen that goes on and on, voices climbing over each other.
Its words, worthy is the Lamb that was slain, come from the fifth chapter of the Apocalypse, where they're sung in heaven, by a choir far bigger than any concert hall could hold.

teach.h: A SCROLL NO ONE CAN OPEN.
teach.b: Chapter five begins with a problem. In the right hand of the one on the throne is a scroll, written inside and out, sealed with seven seals. A strong angel calls out: who is worthy to open it?
No one in heaven or on earth or under the earth can. John weeps much, he says. Then an elder tells him: weep not; the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the root of David, has won, and can open the scroll.

teach.h: TOLD A LION, JOHN SEES A LAMB.
teach.b: John turns to look for a lion, and sees a Lamb. Standing, yet looking as though it had been slain. Told a lion, he sees a lamb with its wounds still showing.

That's the whole book in one image: the power that wins is a love that was killed and is alive. John's Greek word is arnion, which can mean a little lamb. The Lamb takes the scroll, and heaven erupts.
The creatures and the elders fall down with harps and bowls of incense, which the text says are the prayers of the saints.
Thousands upon thousands of angels sing, in the Douay-Rheims: "The Lamb that was slain is worthy to receive power, and divinity, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and benediction."
Then every creature, in heaven, on earth, under the earth and in the sea, joins in. Catholics hear this at Mass.

teach.h: THE LAMB OF GOD AT EVERY MASS.
teach.b: As the host is broken before Communion, the people sing or say the Lamb of God, and the priest holds up the host and says, behold the Lamb of God.

teach.h: THE LAMB THAT WAS SLAIN IS WORTHY.
teach.b: The Catechism says the liturgy on earth already shares in this heavenly one.

how: At every Mass, while the host is broken, the people sing or say the Agnus Dei, Lamb of God, three times, and the priest then shows the host with the words of John the Baptist, Behold the Lamb of God; the Church teaches that the earthly liturgy shares in the heavenly one.

s: Handel's Messiah ends with the Hallelujah chorus
it closes with worthy is the Lamb that was slain and a long Amen, from Apocalypse 5.
John is told about a lion, then turns and sees a lamb
the Lion of Juda has won, and he appears as a Lamb that was slain.
in Apocalypse 5, the incense in the elders' bowls stands for the prayers of the saints
heaven holds the prayers of God's people.

games.q: you're John. no one in heaven or on earth can open the sealed scroll, and you're weeping. an elder says the Lion of Juda has won. you turn around. what do you see?
o: a lamb, standing, as though it had been slain.
games.why: told a lion, John sees a lamb with its wounds still showing. the power that wins is a love that was killed and is alive.

practice: Picture the throne, the scroll, the Lamb standing with its wounds showing, and every creature everywhere singing, and let your own small voice be one of them.
If you pray, say the Agnus Dei slowly, in your own language or the old Latin, Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi, miserere nobis, three times, a breath for each.
If you don't pray, just picture the Lamb, and notice what it means that the winner has wounds.

wordCard.voice: Arnion, a little lamb. Apocalypse five: the lamb standing with its wounds still showing, worthy to open the scroll no one else could open. Today's word.
